sentences.text: Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 14.09.2022 passed in MVC No.6117/2019 by the Court of the MACT, C/C XVI Addl.

Judge Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (for short NC:
2023:KHC:33873 'the Tribunal'), the petitioner/insurance company has preferred MFA.No.8478/2022 and the respondents/legal heirs of the deceased have preferred MFA.No.2007/2023 seeking enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 16.05.2019 at about 8.20 a.m., one Mahadesha was walking on Bannerghatta-Jigani Road and while crossing the road near Mantapa gate, a Maruti Swift car bearing registration No. KA-05-MJ-7713, being driven in a rash and negligent manner and duly insured with respondent No.2-Insurance company, came and dashed against the said Mahadesha, because of which, he sustained grievous injuries.
He preferred MVC.No.6117/2019.
During the pendency of the case, he expired on 28.02.2020.
His legal heirs got impleaded themselves and contended that the death happened due to the injuries sustained by the said Mahadesha in the accident.
The Tribunal based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, concluded that the said Mahadesha, died due to the injuries NC: 2023:KHC:33873 suffered by him during the accident.

Aggrieved by the same, the respondent No.2/Insurance company has preferred MFA.No.8478/2022 and not satisfied by the compensation awarded,
the petitioners have preferred MFA.No.2007/2023.

4. The questions that arise for consideration in the above appeals are:
i. Whether Mahadesha died due to the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
ii. What is the compensation petitioners are entitled to.
5.

The answer to the first question as to the cause for the death of Mahadesha can be found by analyzing the evidence given by P.Ws.3 and 4 and Exs.P.29 and 30.
6.
P.W.3 is the doctor, who has treated the deceased Mahadesha.
As per his evidence, the petitioner sustained orthopedic injuries due to the accident and they have not caused the death of the Sri.

4 petitioner.
However, he has treated the petitioner immediately after the accident and not at the time of the death.
P.W.4 is the doctor, who has conducted postmortem of the body of Mahadesha.
He has not treated the deceased, but has conducted only postmortem of his body after his death.
He has deposed in his evidence, that it is not possible to say the reason for the death till receipt of the FSL report.
As on the date of his deposition, the FSL report was not in received.

8. Ex.P.30 is the FSL report which is dated 16.02.2021 and the relevant portion reads as under:
"The following articles were received here on 03.11.2020 through Grade-I Police Constable 1370 Tr.Venkatesan with proper labels under unbroken seals which corresponded with the sample sent viz:-
1. Stomach and intestine with its contents 2. Liver and Kidney 3. Preservative
The above three (3) articles were examined but alcohol or other poison was not detected in any of them."
9. Based on the FSL report, P.W.4 has given a postmortem certificate wherein he has opined that the cause of death was due to post traumatic sequence.
P.W.7 is the police sub-inspector and in his deposition Exs.P.29 and 30 have been NC: 2023:KHC:33873 marked and he has pleaded ignorance about the contents of the same.
10. After marking of Exs.P.29 and 30, P.W.4 has not been re-examined.
11. The onus of proving that the deceased-Mahadesha died due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident is on the petitioners.
To prove the same, they have examined P.W.3, who has stated that the injuries has not resulted in the death of Mahadesha.

P.W.4, after conducting the postmortem,
has deposed that he cannot say the reason for the death till he receives the FSL report.
The FSL report merely states that the stomach, liver and kidney of the deceased did not contain any alcohol or poison.
It does not mention anything about, the post trauma, causing the death of the deceased.
After receipt of the FSL report, P.W.4 has given a postmortem certificate within an opinion that the cause of death was due to post traumatic sequence.

This opinion of P.W.4 cannot be believed because he has deposed after postmortem that he cannot state the reason for the death till he receives FSL report and the FSL report does NC: 2023:KHC:33873 not reveal the reason for the death and postmortem certificate which is issued has to be considered erroneous.
12. For the above mentioned reasons, it is hereby held that the petitioners have failed to prove the cause of death of the deceased was due to accident.

Under the circumstances, the petitioners are not Sri. Mahadesha vs Sri Hemaraj B. Shetty on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164595825/
5 entitled to compensation for the death of the deceased.

sentences.text: 13. Thus the petitioners under the given facts and circumstances of the case would be entitled to the medical and other incidental expenses that the family would have spent for treating the deceased.
14. The Tribunal, based on the evidence let in, has come to the conclusion that the petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.1,68,200/- towards medical expenses.
I have no reason to differ from the same.
15. However, no compensation is awarded towards food nourishment and attendant charges.

Under the facts and circumstances of the case, I deem it appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards the same.
The Tribunal has awarded interest at the rate of 9% p.a., on the compensation amount.
Given the bank rate of interest, I deem it appropriate to award the same at 6% p.a., from the date of petition before the Trial Court till realization.

17. Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) MFA.No.8478/2022 is allowed in part and MFA.No.2007/2023 is hereby dismissed;
(ii) The petitioners are entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,18,200/- as against Rs.10,77,172/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

(iii) The sum of Rs.2,18,200/- shall be paid by respondent No.2/Insurance company to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition before the Tribunal till realization;
 (iv) The amounts in deposit before this Court shall  be transferred to Tribunal and after disbursement of the compensation amount to the petitioners, excess amount if any shall be - 11 - Sri. (v) Office to draw modified award accordingly;
(vi) Registry to return the records to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.
